about.title: Manteca Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Manteca has grown quickly, and with roughly 75,000 residents now shopping, working, and renting across the city, more people pass through privately owned spaces every day than ever before. Storefronts along Yosemite Avenue and Main Street, commercial centers near the SR-120 and SR-99 interchanges, and the apartment complexes filling in new neighborhoods all share one obligation under California law: keep the property reasonably safe, or warn about what cannot be fixed right away. When a wet floor goes unmarked, a stair rail is loose, or a parking lot stays dark for weeks, the question becomes what the owner knew and when. That notice element decides most Manteca premises cases, and it is why photographs, incident reports, and witness names taken in the first hours matter so much. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery. You focus on healing; the attorney handles the property owner and its insurer.

whyChoose.title: Why Manteca Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Attorneys who know how to prove notice
items.desc: California requires showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network dig into cleaning logs, inspection schedules, and prior complaints to build that record.

items.title: Fast action on surveillance video
items.desc: Many Manteca businesses record their floors and lots, but footage is often overwritten within days. A connected attorney can send preservation demands before the evidence disappears.

items.title: Clear guidance on deadlines and shared fault
items.desc: You generally have two years to file, far less if a public entity is involved, and California's pure comparative fault rule means a claim survives even if you were partly at fault. An attorney sorts this out early so nothing is lost.

items.question: I fell at a shopping center near SR-120 in Manteca and the manager said I should have watched where I was walking. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California follows pure comparative fault, so even if a jury decided you were partly responsible, your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated. The bigger issue is whether the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address or warn about it. An attorney can evaluate both sides of that question with you.

items.question: What if I tripped on a broken sidewalk or fell at a City of Manteca facility?
items.answer: Claims against a city, county, or other public entity follow different rules with a much shorter deadline than the standard two years, and you typically must file a formal government claim before any lawsuit. Missing that window can end the case regardless of how strong it is. Reach out promptly so an attorney can confirm who owns the property and what deadline applies.

items.question: How do I preserve evidence after a slip and fall?
items.answer: Photograph the hazard, your footwear, and the surrounding area before anything is cleaned or repaired, and get names of anyone who saw you fall. Ask for a written incident report and request that any surveillance video be saved, since many systems erase footage within a week or two. Seek medical care right away so your injuries are documented from the start. An attorney connected through LawProactive can follow up with formal preservation letters.
